messages.content: Write REXX to read a dataset and display its contents on z/OS

Here's how to read a sequential dataset or PDS member using EXECIO in z/OS REXX:

```rexx
/* REXX - Read dataset and display contents */
/* Allocate the dataset first */
"ALLOC F(INFILE) DA('YOUR.DATASET.NAME') SHR REUSE"

IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Error allocating dataset, RC=' RC
   EXIT 8
END

/* Read all records into stem variable */
"EXECIO * DISKR INFILE (STEM LINE. FINIS)"
read_rc = RC

/* Free the file */
"FREE F(INFILE)"

IF read_rc \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Error reading dataset, RC=' read_rc
   EXIT 8
END

/* Display each line */
SAY 'Total records read:' LINE.0
SAY ''
DO i = 1 TO LINE.0
   SAY LINE.i
END

EXIT 0
```

Key points:
- ALLOC allocates the dataset to a DDname (INFILE)
- EXECIO * DISKR reads all records into stem variable LINE.
- LINE.0 contains the count of records
- LINE.1, LINE.2, etc. contain the actual data
- FINIS closes the file after reading
- Always FREE the file when done
Write REXX to write data to a dataset on z/OS

Here's how to write data to a sequential dataset using EXECIO in z/OS REXX:

```rexx
/* REXX - Write data to a dataset */
/* Build the output data in a stem */
OUTPUT.1 = 'First line of data'
OUTPUT.2 = 'Second line of data'
OUTPUT.3 = 'Third line of data'
OUTPUT.0 = 3  /* Number of lines */

/* Allocate output dataset - create if new */
"ALLOC F(OUTFILE) DA('YOUR.OUTPUT.DATASET') OLD REUSE"

IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
   /* Try creating new dataset */
   "ALLOC F(OUTFILE) DA('YOUR.OUTPUT.DATASET') NEW CATALOG",
   "SPACE(1,1) TRACKS LRECL(80) RECFM(F,B) BLKSIZE(8000)"
   IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
      SAY 'Cannot allocate output dataset, RC=' RC
      EXIT 8
   END
END

/* Write the stem to the dataset */
"EXECIO" OUTPUT.0 "DISKW OUTFILE (STEM OUTPUT. FINIS)"
write_rc = RC

/* Free the file */
"FREE F(OUTFILE)"

IF write_rc \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Error writing dataset, RC=' write_rc
   EXIT 8
END

SAY 'Successfully wrote' OUTPUT.0 'records'
EXIT 0
```

Key points:
- Build output in stem variable (OUTPUT.1, OUTPUT.2, etc.)
- Set OUTPUT.0 to the count of records
- EXECIO n DISKW writes n records from the stem
- Use FINIS to close the file after writing
How do I execute TSO commands from REXX?

In z/OS REXX, you execute TSO commands by enclosing them in quotes. Here are common patterns:

```rexx
/* REXX - Execute TSO commands */

/* List dataset */
"LISTDS 'SYS1.PARMLIB' MEMBERS"

/* Check return code */
IF RC \= 0 THEN
   SAY 'LISTDS failed with RC=' RC

/* Allocate a dataset */
"ALLOC F(MYFILE) DA('MY.DATA.SET') SHR REUSE"

/* Submit a job */
"SUBMIT 'MY.JCL.LIBRARY(MYJOB)'"
job_rc = RC
SAY 'Submit RC=' job_rc

/* Delete a dataset */
"DELETE 'MY.TEMP.DATASET'"

/* Rename a dataset */
"RENAME 'OLD.NAME' 'NEW.NAME'"

/* Copy a dataset */
"REPRO INFILE(IN) OUTFILE(OUT)"

/* Call another program */
"CALL 'SYS1.LINKLIB(IEFBR14)'"

/* Send message to operator console */
"SEND 'Processing complete' USER(OPER)"

/* Execute ISPF command */
ADDRESS ISPEXEC
"EDIT DATASET('MY.DATA.SET')"
ADDRESS TSO

/* Capture command output using OUTTRAP */
CALL OUTTRAP 'OUT.'
"LISTDS 'SYS1.PROCLIB' MEMBERS"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

DO i = 1 TO OUT.0
   SAY OUT.i
END
```

Key points:
- TSO commands in quotes execute directly
- Check RC after each command
- Use ADDRESS to switch environments (TSO, ISPEXEC, MVS)
- OUTTRAP captures command output
Write REXX to parse a JCL member and extract job information

Here's REXX to read a JCL member and extract key information:

```rexx
/* REXX - Parse JCL and extract job info */
ARG pds_name member_name

IF pds_name = '' THEN DO
   SAY 'Usage: PARSEJCL pds.name member'
   EXIT 4
END

/* Build dataset name */
full_name = "'"pds_name"("member_name")'"

/* Allocate the JCL member */
"ALLOC F(JCLIN) DA("full_name") SHR REUSE"
IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Cannot allocate' full_name
   EXIT 8
END

/* Read all lines */
"EXECIO * DISKR JCLIN (STEM JCL. FINIS)"
"FREE F(JCLIN)"

/* Initialize counters */
job_count = 0
step_count = 0
dd_count = 0

/* Parse each line */
DO i = 1 TO JCL.0
   line = JCL.i
   
   /* Skip comments and empty lines */
   IF SUBSTR(line,1,3) = '//*' THEN ITERATE
   IF STRIP(line) = '' THEN ITERATE
   
   /* Check for JOB card */
   IF POS(' JOB ',line) > 0 THEN DO
      job_count = job_count + 1
      PARSE VAR line '//' jobname ' JOB ' rest
      SAY 'JOB:' STRIP(jobname)
   END
   
   /* Check for EXEC statement */
   IF POS(' EXEC ',line) > 0 THEN DO
      step_count = step_count + 1
      PARSE VAR line '//' stepname ' EXEC ' pgm_info
      SAY '  STEP:' STRIP(stepname) '-' STRIP(pgm_info)
   END
   
   /* Check for DD statement */
   IF POS(' DD ',line) > 0 THEN DO
      dd_count = dd_count + 1
      PARSE VAR line '//' ddname ' DD ' dd_info
      SAY '    DD:' STRIP(ddname)
   END
END

SAY ''
SAY 'Summary:'
SAY '  Jobs:' job_count
SAY '  Steps:' step_count
SAY '  DD statements:' dd_count

EXIT 0
```

This parses JCL and extracts:
- JOB names
- EXEC steps and programs
- DD statements
How do I use ISPF services from REXX?

Here's how to use ISPF services from REXX on z/OS:

```rexx
/* REXX - Using ISPF Services */
ADDRESS ISPEXEC

/* Display a panel */
"DISPLAY PANEL(MYPANEL)"
IF RC > 8 THEN DO
   SAY 'Panel display error, RC=' RC
   EXIT 8
END

/* Set and get ISPF variables */
"VPUT (VAR1 VAR2) PROFILE"  /* Save to profile */
"VGET (VAR1 VAR2) PROFILE"  /* Retrieve from profile */

/* Edit a dataset */
dsname = 'MY.DATA.SET'
"EDIT DATASET('"dsname"')"
edit_rc = RC
SELECT
   WHEN edit_rc = 0 THEN SAY 'Edit saved'
   WHEN edit_rc = 4 THEN SAY 'Edit cancelled'
   OTHERWISE SAY 'Edit error, RC=' edit_rc
END

/* Browse a dataset */
"BROWSE DATASET('SYS1.PARMLIB(IEASYS00)')"

/* View a dataset (read-only edit) */
"VIEW DATASET('MY.DATA.SET')"

/* Use table services */
"TBCREATE MYTABLE KEYS(KEY1) NAMES(FLD1 FLD2 FLD3) NOWRITE"

/* Add rows to table */
DO i = 1 TO 5
   KEY1 = 'KEY'i
   FLD1 = 'Data'i
   FLD2 = i * 100
   FLD3 = DATE()
   "TBADD MYTABLE"
END

/* Display table */
"TBDISPL MYTABLE PANEL(TBPANEL)"

/* Close table */
"TBEND MYTABLE"

/* File tailoring - build output from skeleton */
"FTOPEN TEMP"
"FTINCL MYSKEL"   /* Include skeleton */
"FTCLOSE NAME(OUTPUT)"

/* Submit job from file tailoring output */
"VGET (ZTEMPF) SHARED"
ADDRESS TSO "SUBMIT '"ZTEMPF"'"

/* Log a message */
"LOG MSG(PROC001I) 'Processing started'"

/* Library access */
"LMINIT DATAID(DID) DATASET('MY.PDS') ENQ(SHRW)"
"LMOPEN DATAID("DID") OPTION(INPUT)"
"LMMLIST DATAID("DID") OPTION(LIST) MEMBER(MEM)"
DO WHILE RC = 0
   SAY 'Member:' MEM
   "LMMLIST DATAID("DID") OPTION(LIST) MEMBER(MEM)"
END
"LMCLOSE DATAID("DID")"
"LMFREE DATAID("DID")"

EXIT 0
```

Key ISPF services:
- DISPLAY/TBDISPL: Show panels/tables
- EDIT/BROWSE/VIEW: Dataset editing
- VPUT/VGET: Variable storage
- TB*: Table services
- LM*: Library access
- FT*: File tailoring
Write REXX to check if a dataset exists on z/OS

Here are several ways to check if a dataset exists in z/OS REXX:

```rexx
/* REXX - Check if dataset exists */

/* Method 1: Using SYSDSN function (simplest) */
dsname = 'SYS1.PARMLIB'
result = SYSDSN("'"dsname"'")

IF result = 'OK' THEN
   SAY dsname 'exists'
ELSE
   SAY dsname 'not found:' result

/* SYSDSN returns:
   OK              - Dataset exists
   MEMBER NOT FOUND - PDS exists but member doesn't
   DATASET NOT FOUND - Dataset doesn't exist
   ERROR PROCESSING REQUESTED DATASET
   UNAVAILABLE DATASET - Dataset in use exclusively
   and others...
*/

/* Method 2: Using LISTDSI function (more info) */
dsname = 'SYS1.PROCLIB'
result = LISTDSI("'"dsname"'")

IF result = 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Dataset:' SYSDSNAME
   SAY 'Volume:' SYSVOLUME
   SAY 'Organization:' SYSDSORG
   SAY 'Record format:' SYSRECFM
   SAY 'Record length:' SYSLRECL
   SAY 'Block size:' SYSBLKSIZE
   SAY 'Used space:' SYSUSED 'tracks'
END
ELSE DO
   SAY 'LISTDSI failed, RC=' result
   SAY 'Reason:' SYSMSGLVL2
END

/* Method 3: Using ALLOC to test */
dsname = 'MY.DATA.SET'
"ALLOC F(TEST) DA('"dsname"') SHR REUSE"
IF RC = 0 THEN DO
   SAY dsname 'exists and is accessible'
   "FREE F(TEST)"
END
ELSE
   SAY dsname 'does not exist or not accessible'

/* Method 4: Check PDS member existence */
pds = 'SYS1.PROCLIB'
member = 'JES2'

result = SYSDSN("'"pds"("member")'") 
IF result = 'OK' THEN
   SAY 'Member' member 'exists in' pds
ELSE
   SAY 'Member' member 'not found:' result

/* Practical function to check existence */
CheckDS: PROCEDURE
   ARG dsname
   result = SYSDSN("'"dsname"'")
   IF result = 'OK' THEN RETURN 1
   RETURN 0

/* Usage */
IF CheckDS('SYS1.LINKLIB') THEN
   SAY 'LINKLIB exists'
ELSE
   SAY 'LINKLIB not found'

EXIT 0
```

Best practices:
- Use SYSDSN for simple existence check
- Use LISTDSI for detailed dataset info
- Always quote dataset names with single quotes
- Check for specific SYSDSN return values
Write REXX to capture and process console command output

Here's how to capture TSO/console command output using OUTTRAP in z/OS REXX:

```rexx
/* REXX - Capture command output with OUTTRAP */

/* Enable output trapping to stem variable */
CALL OUTTRAP 'OUT.'

/* Execute command - output goes to stem */
"LISTDS 'SYS1.PARMLIB' MEMBERS"

/* Disable trapping */
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

/* Process captured output */
SAY 'Captured' OUT.0 'lines of output'
SAY ''

DO i = 1 TO OUT.0
   SAY OUT.i
END

/* Practical example: Find specific member */
CALL OUTTRAP 'MEM.'
"LISTDS 'SYS1.PROCLIB' MEMBERS"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

/* Search for a member */
search_member = 'JES2'
found = 0

DO i = 1 TO MEM.0
   IF POS(search_member, MEM.i) > 0 THEN DO
      SAY 'Found:' STRIP(MEM.i)
      found = 1
   END
END

IF \found THEN
   SAY search_member 'not found'

/* Example: Get system information */
CALL OUTTRAP 'SYS.'
ADDRESS TSO "STATUS"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

SAY 'System Status:'
DO i = 1 TO SYS.0
   SAY '  ' SYS.i
END

/* Example: Parse LISTCAT output */
CALL OUTTRAP 'CAT.'
"LISTCAT ENT('MY.DATA.**') NAME"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

dsn_count = 0
DO i = 1 TO CAT.0
   line = STRIP(CAT.i)
   IF POS('NONVSAM', line) > 0 | POS('CLUSTER', line) > 0 THEN DO
      PARSE VAR line type '---' dsname
      IF dsname \= '' THEN DO
         dsn_count = dsn_count + 1
         SAY dsn_count':' STRIP(dsname)
      END
   END
END

SAY 'Total datasets found:' dsn_count

/* Advanced: Capture with line limit */
CALL OUTTRAP 'OUT.', 100, 'NOCONCAT'  /* Max 100 lines, don't append */
"LISTDS 'SYS1.**' MEMBERS"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

IF OUT.0 = 100 THEN
   SAY 'Warning: Output may be truncated'

EXIT 0
```

OUTTRAP syntax:
- CALL OUTTRAP 'stem.' - Start capturing
- CALL OUTTRAP 'stem.', n - Limit to n lines
- CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF' - Stop capturing
- stem.0 = count of lines
- stem.1, stem.2, etc. = captured lines
Write REXX to process a VSAM file on z/OS

Here's how to read and process VSAM files using REXX on z/OS:

```rexx
/* REXX - Process VSAM KSDS file */
vsam_file = 'MY.VSAM.KSDS'

/* Allocate VSAM file */
"ALLOC F(VSAMFILE) DA('"vsam_file"') SHR REUSE"
IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Error allocating VSAM file, RC=' RC
   EXIT 8
END

/* Read all records */
"EXECIO * DISKR VSAMFILE (STEM REC. FINIS)"
read_rc = RC

"FREE F(VSAMFILE)"

IF read_rc \= 0 & read_rc \= 2 THEN DO
   SAY 'Error reading VSAM, RC=' read_rc
   EXIT 8
END

SAY 'Read' REC.0 'records from VSAM file'

/* Process each record */
DO i = 1 TO REC.0
   record = REC.i
   /* Parse fixed-format record */
   key = SUBSTR(record, 1, 8)
   name = SUBSTR(record, 9, 30)
   amount = SUBSTR(record, 39, 10)
   
   SAY 'Key:' key 'Name:' STRIP(name) 'Amount:' amount
END

EXIT 0
```

**Write to VSAM:**
```rexx
/* REXX - Write to VSAM KSDS */
vsam_file = 'MY.VSAM.KSDS'

/* Build records */
NEW.1 = LEFT('KEY00001', 8) || LEFT('JOHN SMITH', 30) || RIGHT('1000.00', 10)
NEW.2 = LEFT('KEY00002', 8) || LEFT('JANE DOE', 30) || RIGHT('2500.00', 10)
NEW.0 = 2

/* Allocate for output */
"ALLOC F(VSAMOUT) DA('"vsam_file"') OLD REUSE"
IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Cannot allocate VSAM, RC=' RC
   EXIT 8
END

/* Write records */
"EXECIO" NEW.0 "DISKW VSAMOUT (STEM NEW. FINIS)"
write_rc = RC

"FREE F(VSAMOUT)"

IF write_rc \= 0 THEN DO
   SAY 'Write error, RC=' write_rc
   EXIT 8
END

SAY 'Wrote' NEW.0 'records'
EXIT 0
```

**Using IDCAMS from REXX:**
```rexx
/* REXX - Call IDCAMS for VSAM operations */

/* Delete and define VSAM cluster */
CALL OUTTRAP 'OUT.'
"IDCAMS" 
"  DELETE MY.VSAM.CLUSTER PURGE"
"  DEFINE CLUSTER(NAME(MY.VSAM.CLUSTER) -"
"    INDEXED KEYS(8 0) -"
"    RECORDSIZE(100 100) -"
"    CYLINDERS(5 1)) -"
"  DATA(NAME(MY.VSAM.DATA)) -"
"  INDEX(NAME(MY.VSAM.INDEX))"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

DO i = 1 TO OUT.0
   SAY OUT.i
END

/* Print VSAM info */
CALL OUTTRAP 'INFO.'
"LISTCAT ENT('MY.VSAM.CLUSTER') ALL"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

DO i = 1 TO INFO.0
   SAY INFO.i  
END

EXIT 0
```

Key points:
- VSAM files use same EXECIO as sequential
- RC=2 means EOF (normal for reads)
- Use OLD for update, SHR for read
- IDCAMS for define/delete/repro operations
Write a complete REXX program for batch job monitoring on z/OS

Here's a comprehensive REXX program for monitoring batch jobs on z/OS:

```rexx
/* REXX - Batch Job Monitor */
/**********************************************************************/
/* JOBMON - Monitor batch job status and performance                  */
/* Usage: JOBMON jobname | JOBMON jobname* | JOBMON ALL               */
/**********************************************************************/
ARG job_pattern

IF job_pattern = '' THEN job_pattern = '*'

SAY COPIES('=', 70)
SAY 'JOB MONITOR - ' DATE() TIME()
SAY COPIES('=', 70)
SAY ''

/* Get job information using STATUS command */
CALL OUTTRAP 'JOBS.'
IF job_pattern = 'ALL' THEN
   "STATUS"
ELSE
   "STATUS" job_pattern
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

/* Parse and display job information */
job_count = 0
active_count = 0

DO i = 1 TO JOBS.0
   line = JOBS.i
   
   /* Skip header lines */
   IF POS('NO JOBS', line) > 0 THEN DO
      SAY 'No matching jobs found'
      LEAVE
   END
   
   IF POS('JOB', line) > 0 & POS('STEP', line) > 0 THEN DO
      job_count = job_count + 1
      
      /* Parse job line */
      PARSE VAR line jobname 'JOB' jobnum rest
      
      /* Check if job is active */
      IF POS('EXECUTING', line) > 0 THEN DO
         active_count = active_count + 1
         status = 'ACTIVE'
      END
      ELSE IF POS('WAITING', line) > 0 THEN
         status = 'WAITING'
      ELSE IF POS('HELD', line) > 0 THEN
         status = 'HELD'
      ELSE
         status = 'UNKNOWN'
      
      SAY LEFT(STRIP(jobname), 8) 'JOB' LEFT(jobnum, 8) status
   END
END

SAY ''
SAY COPIES('-', 40)
SAY 'Total jobs:' job_count
SAY 'Active:' active_count
SAY COPIES('-', 40)

/* Optional: Get spool information for active jobs */
IF active_count > 0 THEN DO
   SAY ''
   SAY 'Checking spool output...'
   
   CALL OUTTRAP 'SPOOL.'
   "OUTPUT" job_pattern "(PRINT KEEP)"
   CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'
   
   spool_count = 0
   DO i = 1 TO SPOOL.0
      IF POS('SYSOUT', SPOOL.i) > 0 | POS('JESMSGLG', SPOOL.i) > 0 THEN DO
         spool_count = spool_count + 1
         SAY '  ' SPOOL.i
      END
   END
   
   IF spool_count = 0 THEN
      SAY '  No spool output available'
END

/* Get system resource usage */
SAY ''
SAY 'System Resources:'
SAY COPIES('-', 40)

/* Check initiator status */
CALL OUTTRAP 'INIT.'
"D A,L"
CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'

DO i = 1 TO INIT.0
   IF POS('INIT', INIT.i) > 0 | POS('ACTIVE', INIT.i) > 0 THEN
      SAY '  ' INIT.i
END

SAY ''
SAY COPIES('=', 70)
SAY 'Monitor complete'
SAY COPIES('=', 70)

EXIT 0

/**********************************************************************/
/* Subroutine: Get detailed job info                                  */
/**********************************************************************/
GetJobInfo: PROCEDURE
   ARG jobname
   
   CALL OUTTRAP 'INFO.'
   "STATUS" jobname
   CALL OUTTRAP 'OFF'
   
   RETURN INFO.0
```

This program:
- Accepts job name pattern (wildcards supported)
- Shows job status (ACTIVE/WAITING/HELD)
- Counts active jobs
- Checks spool output
- Displays system resource info
- Can be run from TSO or batch
How do I handle errors in REXX on z/OS?

Here's comprehensive error handling in z/OS REXX:

```rexx
/* REXX - Error Handling Examples */

/* Enable condition traps */
SIGNAL ON ERROR    /* Trap command errors */
SIGNAL ON FAILURE  /* Trap command failures */
SIGNAL ON SYNTAX   /* Trap syntax errors */
SIGNAL ON NOVALUE  /* Trap undefined variables */

/* Main processing */
CALL MainProcess
SAY 'Processing completed successfully'
EXIT 0

/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
MainProcess:
/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
   /* Method 1: Check RC after each command */
   "ALLOC F(MYFILE) DA('MY.DATA.SET') SHR REUSE"
   IF RC \= 0 THEN DO
      SAY 'Allocation failed, RC=' RC
      CALL ErrorExit 8, 'ALLOC failed'
   END
   
   /* Method 2: Use SELECT for multiple conditions */
   "EXECIO * DISKR MYFILE (STEM DATA. FINIS)"
   SELECT
      WHEN RC = 0 THEN NOP  /* Success */
      WHEN RC = 2 THEN NOP  /* EOF - normal */
      WHEN RC = 1 THEN CALL ErrorExit 8, 'Data truncated'
      WHEN RC = 4 THEN CALL ErrorExit 8, 'Empty file'
      OTHERWISE CALL ErrorExit 8, 'EXECIO error RC='RC
   END
   
   "FREE F(MYFILE)"
   
   /* Method 3: Capture and analyze return info */
   dsn = 'MAYBE.EXISTS'
   result = SYSDSN("'"dsn"'")
   SELECT
      WHEN result = 'OK' THEN
         SAY 'Dataset exists'
      WHEN result = 'DATASET NOT FOUND' THEN
         SAY 'Dataset not found - will create'
      WHEN result = 'UNAVAILABLE DATASET' THEN DO
         SAY 'Dataset in use - retry later'
         CALL ErrorExit 4, 'Dataset unavailable'
      END
      OTHERWISE DO
         SAY 'Unexpected result:' result
         CALL ErrorExit 8, result
      END
   END
   
   /* Method 4: Trap-based error handling */
   SIGNAL OFF NOVALUE  /* Temporarily disable */
   
   /* Test if variable exists */
   IF SYMBOL('MYVAR') = 'VAR' THEN
      SAY 'MYVAR =' MYVAR
   ELSE
      SAY 'MYVAR not defined'
   
   SIGNAL ON NOVALUE   /* Re-enable */
   
   RETURN

/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
ErrorExit:
/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
   PARSE ARG exit_rc, error_msg
   SAY '*** ERROR:' error_msg
   SAY '*** Exiting with RC=' exit_rc
   
   /* Cleanup before exit */
   CALL Cleanup
   
   EXIT exit_rc

/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
Cleanup:
/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
   /* Free any allocated files */
   "FREE F(MYFILE)" 
   "FREE F(OUTFILE)"
   RETURN

/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* Signal handlers                                                    */
/*--------------------------------------------------------------------*/
ERROR:
   SAY '*** Command error at line' SIGL
   SAY '*** Command:' SOURCELINE(SIGL)
   SAY '*** RC=' RC
   CALL Cleanup
   EXIT 16

FAILURE:
   SAY '*** Command failure at line' SIGL
   SAY '*** Command:' SOURCELINE(SIGL)  
   CALL Cleanup
   EXIT 20

SYNTAX:
   SAY '*** Syntax error at line' SIGL
   SAY '*** Error:' ERRORTEXT(RC)
   SAY '*** Source:' SOURCELINE(SIGL)
   CALL Cleanup
   EXIT 24

NOVALUE:
   SAY '*** Undefined variable at line' SIGL
   SAY '*** Variable:' CONDITION('D')
   SAY '*** Source:' SOURCELINE(SIGL)
   CALL Cleanup
   EXIT 28
```

Key error handling techniques:
- Check RC after every command
- Use SIGNAL ON for trap handlers
- SELECT for multiple conditions
- Create ErrorExit routine for cleanup
- SIGL gives error line number
- SOURCELINE() shows the code
- ERRORTEXT() describes syntax errors
